First off, there is no draft.

What you register for is "Selective Service". It's nothing more than a database of eligible aged people (men). If ever there was some kind of horrible, protracted conflict in which conscripted troops were necessary, it takes a full-on act of congress to create, activate or reinstate any kind of "draft" or conscription protocol, which would then reference the formerly arbitrary Selective service database. If for whatever reason this database went away, they could just as easily use school registration records, voter registrations, drivers license DB's, tax returns, etc. The SS DB is just another list of names cross referenced with birthdays from a time before all of these various systems could be made to talk to each other.

Now, that being said, either everyone should have to register, or noone should. If you're a woman and you have strong anti-military, pacifist or moral issues with the slim chance of forced military service, you can rail against the system until your heart's content and nothing will befall you. You have no stake in the game, and you lose nothing for following your convictions. If you're a man and you try to put those same convictions into practice, you are penalized the following ways:

  • You are prohibited from applying for government employment,
  • Receiving federal student aid and grants are closed to you
  • You cannot access Federal job training programs
  • You cannot apply for citizenship
  • There is a quarter million dollar fine and potentially 5 years of jail time.
  • Some states have additional penalties as well.

There is no middle ground here. If you advocate for "equal treatment under the law" then you need to pick a side, because allowing Selective Service registration to continue to be male only makes you a hypocrite.
